title: Energy Landscape Sampling Reveals Ligand-Dependent Structural Dynamics of the Protease-Activated Receptor 1.
authors: Schwerin, Inken Kaja; Jiang, Shihai; Staubert, Claudia; Isermann, Berend; Kunze, Georg
journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
one_liner_zh: 该文用增强采样分子动力学（string method）计算PAR1受体五种配体状态下的自由能景观，揭示配体依赖的构象激活路径，属于蛋白质构象采样与结构动态计算研究，方法创新且直接命中课题。
abstract: Protease-activated receptor 1 (PAR1) is a class A G protein-coupled receptor activated by proteolytic cleavage and exposure of a tethered agonist. While existing structures have revealed inactive and active conformations, the ligand-dependent conformational energy landscape governing PAR1 activation remains poorly understood. Here, we employed enhanced-sampling molecular dynamics simulations using the string method with swarms of trajectories to quantify how extracellular ligands and G-protein binding modulate PAR1 activation. Free-energy landscapes were computed for five receptor states (apo, tethered agonist, thrombin receptor-activating peptide (TRAP), vorapaxar (VPX), and VPX + Na+) using five transmembrane (TM) helix distance metrics as collective variables. In the apo state, PAR1 samples inactive, intermediate, and active-like conformations, indicating substantial intrinsic receptor flexibility. VPX increases the free energy of active conformations and restricts TM helix 5 and 6 rearrangements, while VPX + Na+ eliminates intermediate basins and stabilizes the inactive state. In contrast, the tethered agonist stabilizes the active state as the global minimum and promotes TM6 displacement of up to  approximately 1 nm. The simulations reveal a continuous activation pathway linking extracellular ligand engagement to intracellular motifs, including the connector, DRF, intracellular loop 3 (ICL3), and KRK motifs, with intracellular chloride ion coordination contributing to inactive-state stabilization. Galphaq binding reduces TM6 flexibility and shifts the free-energy minimum toward more active-like conformations. Alanine mutagenesis and Gq-CASE BRET assays validate predicted roles of key residues in activation and G-protein coupling. Together, these results provide a detailed understanding of ligand- and transducer-dependent PAR1 signaling and inform the design of pathway-selective PAR1 modulators.
abstract_zh: 蛋白酶激活受体1（PAR1）是一种A类G蛋白偶联受体，通过蛋白水解切割和暴露系留激动剂而被激活。尽管现有结构已揭示非活性和活性构象，但调控PAR1激活的配体依赖性构象能量景观仍知之甚少。在此，我们采用增强采样分子动力学模拟，结合串行方法（string method）与轨迹群（swarms of trajectories），量化细胞外配体和G蛋白结合如何调节PAR1激活。针对五种受体状态（apo、系留激动剂、凝血酶受体激活肽（TRAP）、vorapaxar（VPX）和VPX + Na+），使用五种跨膜（TM）螺旋距离度量作为集合变量计算了自由能景观。在apo状态下，PAR1采样非活性、中间和类活性构象，表明其具有显著的内在受体灵活性。VPX增加活性构象的自由能并限制TM螺旋5和6的重排，而VPX + Na+消除中间盆地并稳定非活性状态。相比之下，系留激动剂将活性状态稳定为全局最小值，并促进TM6位移达约1 nm。模拟揭示了一条连续的激活通路，将细胞外配体结合与细胞内基序（包括connector、DRF、细胞内环3（ICL3）和KRK基序）联系起来，其中细胞内氯离子配位有助于非活性状态的稳定。Galphaq结合降低TM6灵活性，并将自由能最小值向更类活性构象转移。丙氨酸突变和Gq-CASE BRET实验验证了关键残基在激活和G蛋白偶联中的预测作用。综合这些结果，提供了对配体和转导子依赖性PAR1信号传导的详细理解，并为设计通路选择性PAR1调节剂提供信息。
